newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's National Property Trust to list on NZSE.
newsitem.headline: NZ's National Property Trust to list on NZSE.

text.p: National Property Trust said on Wednesday it planned to list on the New Zealand Stock Exchange next month and forecast a net surplus after tax of $1.83 million in the year to May 1997.
NPT said earlier this month that with shareholders approving a NZ$9 million capital raising, it would proceed with a placement and a one-for-four renounceable cash issue.
Unitholders will be offered the issue at 90 cents per unit. Up to one million extra units will be offered. Unitholders have approved the purchase of Hewlett Packard House in Wellington.
NPT published a prospectus forecasting a net surplus after tax for distribution of $1.83 million in the year to May 31, 1997, rising to $2.06 million in the following year.
The net surplus for the year to May 1996 was $1.02 million.
Total income in the 1997 year was forecast in the prospectus at $4.01 million, rising to $4.78 million in the year to May 1998. The listing is set for December 23.
Following the capital raising, the trust would have total assets of $37.58 million. Investors' funds are projected to be $26.19 million.

Annualised pretax returns are projected to be 10.17 cents per unit in 1997 and 10.06 cents the following year. This would put pretax earnings yields on the 90c issue price of new units at 11.30 percent and 11.18 percent.
